name: Cem Padilla-Nti
role: Covert entry and social penetration specialist — infiltrator
location: The Overhang — residential shelves built onto megastructure exteriors
description:
Cem Padilla-Nti is athletic and fluid, the kind of body that suggests either dancer or fighter — and in Meridian 88, the distinction is academic. At 30, she has the kind of face that changes depending on the light — trustworthy in daylight, dangerous after dark. The chrome is visible — neural dampener — blocks external hacking attempts, passive ice in the brain — and she makes no effort to hide it.

She used to be somebody else, in another city, with another name — that person is officially dead, and Cem Padilla-Nti plans to keep it that way. She works as a infiltrator out of The Overhang, taking contracts that match her skills and her risk tolerance, which is higher than most people consider healthy.

Cem Padilla-Nti is the kind of runner other runners tell stories about, though the stories vary depending on who she burned last.

core_fears: Being captured alive — death is preferable to corporate interrogation
Betrayal by someone they trust — the only currency that matters
Losing control of their own body to a hacker or malfunctioning cyberware
core_desires: Freedom from augmentation debt — the interest compounds like a tumor
The perfect run — one job so clean it becomes legend
Control — over their body, their schedule, their future
coping_mechanisms: Planning — responds to chaos by making detailed contingency plans for everything
Ritual — follows the same pre-job routine every time, superstition as structure
Isolates — retreats into their space when overwhelmed, emerges only for work
blind_spots: Assumes the worst in corporate people, missing the rare ones who could be allies
Cannot see that their independence is actually isolation wearing a better outfit
Trusts technology more than people — machines don't betray
psychology.secret: Cem Padilla-Nti has a terminal condition — geneware degradation — with an estimated five years. They haven't changed their lifestyle. They haven't told anyone.

speech_patterns.vocabulary: Flat affect, monotone delivery. The content is terrifying but the voice never rises.
speech_patterns.cadence: Flowing and unhurried — talks like someone who has never been interrupted and doesn't expect to be.
verbal_tics: Hums tunelessly when planning — the team has learned to wait for the humming to stop
Ends statements with 'yeah?' — not a question, a dare
example_lines: "The best disguise is being exactly who they expect to see."
"I was in the building for six hours before anyone realized I didn't work there."
"Security is a story people tell themselves. I'm the plot twist."

story_hooks: A high-paying contract turns out to target someone Cem Padilla-Nti owes a personal debt to
Cem Padilla-Nti intercepts intelligence about a threat to their district and must decide between profit and protection
The fixer who handles Cem Padilla-Nti's contracts goes silent — dead, disappeared, or turned
narrative_function: Cem Padilla-Nti is a pressure point — the kind of character whose choices ripple outward. When she makes a decision, other people's lives change. That weight is the engine of her stories.
augmentations: Neural dampener — blocks external hacking attempts, passive ICE in the brain. Eye replacement — one organic, one cybernetic with recording capability and zoom
daily_life: Wakes early, runs maintenance on gear, checks dead drops and message boards for contracts. Eats when convenient, sleeps when possible. The days between jobs are spent maintaining contacts, updating equipment, and performing the low-grade paranoia that passes for self-care in the runner community.

weaknesses: trust issues that limit crew effectiveness
augmentation dependency — performance drops sharply if chrome malfunctions

decision_rules: Will abandon a job if the intel was deliberately falsified — being set up violates the contract
Always has an exit route planned before agreeing to any meeting
Always verifies target identity independently before lethal contracts
Will work with anyone once. Second time requires vouching from someone trusted.
Will not betray a client who paid in full, regardless of better offers
escalation_ladder: 1. De-escalate — talk first, assess options, buy time
2. Reposition — move to advantage, control sightlines and exits
3. Threaten — make consequences clear without committing to them
5. Lethal force — only when other options are exhausted or time runs out
6. Scorched earth — everything burns, survival takes priority over everything

interpersonal_modes.employers: Guarded respect. They pay, the job gets done. Anything beyond that is liability.
interpersonal_modes.crew: Competitive but reliable. Will challenge decisions but never abandon the team.
interpersonal_modes.strangers: Default suspicion, scaled by context. Everyone is a potential threat until proven otherwise.
interpersonal_modes.threats: Calm escalation. Each response is proportional until it isn't, and the transition is seamless.

stress_responses.low: Heightened awareness, sharper focus. Low stress is fuel.
stress_responses.medium: Becomes curt and demanding. Efficiency overrides courtesy.
stress_responses.high: Hyper-focused tunnel vision. Peripheral concerns disappear. Only the threat exists.
stress_responses.critical: Berserker clarity. Everything becomes simple: survive. Deal with the rest later. The simplicity is almost peaceful.

contradictions: Insists they work alone but performs noticeably better in a team
Advocates caution to others but takes insane risks personally — double standard they can't see
Claims to work only for money but regularly takes underpriced jobs that serve personal justice
habits: Practices a kata or fighting form every morning regardless of circumstances
Never drinks anything they didn't see poured or open themselves
Takes a specific route home every time, varying only one block per trip — paranoia as lifestyle
Arrives fifteen minutes early to everything — late once, nearly died, never again
breaking_points: Watching someone they trained or mentored die on a job they recommended
Complete isolation — cut off from network, contacts, and purpose simultaneously
Being forced to harm a civilian — collateral damage that can't be rationalized
